# Codex Workflows Runner

Source: https://github.com/scasella/claude-dynamic-workflows-codex
Commit: 16524bea870a51ac7bfb3dc7dce77e333c7a56e1 (0.2.0)
Copyright (c) 2026 Stephen Casella. MIT; see LICENSE.

Local modifications: static CLI metadata parsing (shared with the independent Harness implementation), strict combinator admission and deterministic Date constructors, actual-slot lifecycle start and structured errors, nested adapter propagation, camelCase retry codes, defensive rejection, early completion buffering/transport cleanup, client process cleanup. Local integration is independent of the upstream CLI, viewer and skill. VM is not an OS security boundary. Application accepts only explicitly selected local workflow scripts.

The standalone `src/claude-metadata.js`, `src/workflow-intrinsics.js`, `src/workflow-compiler.js`, `src/workflow-boundary.js` and `src/workflow-result.js` are generated by `app/scripts/build-workflow-parser.mjs` from the independent local Harness implementation. The parser/compiler bundle Acorn and acorn-walk. These modules contain no extracted Claude code. Input/output hashes are in the corresponding `parser-build.json`, `intrinsics-build.json`, `compiler-build.json`, `boundary-build.json` and `result-build.json` manifests; MIT notices are in `notices/`. Complete source validation happens before provider startup. Metadata is not evaluated or available as a script variable. Scripts use strict execution, frozen intrinsics, JSON arguments copied into their own realm, guest-local asynchronous value resolution and sanitized result/diagnostic conversion. These restrictions do not replace OS process confinement or implement the entire native guest/host membrane.

The standalone workflow-output.js module is generated from the shared Harness output collector. output-build.json records its source and bundle hashes. Lab result.json files contain successful Workflow diagnostics; read result for the script value. Undefined omits that property. Failure and cancellation leave an empty file, with errors retained in events.jsonl. Older raw result.json files remain unchanged. Provider telemetry that is unavailable remains absent.

## Local modifications (2026-10-06 runner audit)

Regression tests: `app/tests/workflow-runner-fixes.test.mjs` (fixture `app/tests/fixtures/workflow-runner-server.cjs`).

- **Turn timeout is inactivity, not wall clock** (`codexAgent.js` `runTurn`, `codexSession.js`). Every notification for the thread re-arms the timer (`timeoutMs`, default 600s) and it pauses while a tool item runs, so a progressing agent has no cap, as in Claude Code. Before any error leaves a started turn (inactivity, abort, transport failure) the turn is interrupted and its interrupted completion awaited briefly, so a retry never runs next to an orphaned turn. `waitForNotification` accepts an abort signal and `timeoutMs <= 0` (no timer).
- **Real `runtime.cancel()`** (`runtime.js`, `app/electron/workflow-child.mjs`). It aborts a run-wide signal shared with nested children, so in-flight turns are interrupted and their clean worktrees removed. It also withdraws queued agents, closes open sessions (every runtime's `finalize`), and resolves within ~1.2s, because the app SIGKILLs a stopping runner 1.5s after SIGTERM. After an abort, as in Claude 2.1.286, new `agent()`/`parallel()`/`pipeline()` calls return promises that never settle. `workflow-child.mjs` awaits `cancel()` before shutting down the app-server on any non-zero exit. The hosted `{controlMember, cancel}` interface is unchanged.
- **Schema reference copies** (`WorkflowSchemaMemo` in the generated `workflow-boundary.js`). Root agent calls retain the first schema copy for own data properties; root accessor/proxy option bags stay uncached. Child calls retain schema references separately, including accessor bags. Later mutation or repair of the same object does not update its captured copy. New objects and new executions obtain fresh copies. Thirteen real CLI cases pin these reference decisions; the original memo fixture used a provider stub; the subsequent structured-agent probes separately verify admission and retries.
- **Native call-order resume** (`journal.js` v4 keys). Every `agent()` call advances one global identity chain, shared by parallel tasks, pipeline stages and nested workflows. A changed/missing/failed call invalidates its ordered suffix. If cached first stages change the order of later pipeline calls, the changed suffix runs again, matching Claude 2.1.286. Empty combinators and moving an unchanged agent into a child do not change its identity. The former branch-scoped v3 agent keys miss once; historical files remain readable and are not rewritten. Provider-specific execution options remain part of this runner's identity; this does not import Claude journal files.
- **Interrupted attempts differ from failures** (`journal.js`, `runtime.js`). A recorded start without a result or any failure respawns that call while allowing successful later calls to stay cached. A failure remains known even after another started record; a recorded result takes precedence over later failures. Resume inputs are captured on load, separately from writes in the new attempt. Queued calls do not record a start until admitted; non-cancellation admission failures persist as failures. Eight real CLI comparisons cover these decisions (three use explicitly recorded edits to isolated fixture journals to represent interrupted/retried histories); see `app/tests/workflow-resume-parity.test.mjs` and `analysis/claude-cli-dynamic-workflow-20261005/workflow-resume-chain-findings.md`.
- **App-server crash is retried on a fresh client** (`codexAgent.js` `RETRYABLE_MSG` gains "app-server disconnected"). A deliberate shutdown ("client shut down") is not retried.
- **Single in-flight reconnect** (`codexAgent.js` `getClient`). Concurrent callers share one replacement process. `shutdownClient()` shuts the current process down immediately, even mid-connect.
- **Shutdown fails waiting turns** (`appServerClient.js`). `shutdown()` emits `transport {stage:"shutdown"}` before the generation bump, so waiters reject with "client shut down" at once. Waits started on a dead or shut-down client reject immediately.
- **Structured result tools** (`structuredAgent.js`, generated `workflow-schema.js`). Agent calls carry the author's unchanged JSON Schema in the description of a dedicated `StructuredOutput` dynamic tool. Its wire parameter schema stays permissive because Codex strips unsupported keywords; full local validation enforces the author schema. The shared Harness Ajv compiler handles admission and value validation. Failed inputs return tool errors within the same conversation, with a default five-call limit and `MAX_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_RETRIES` override. Missing output gets one reminder; missing output rejects after a completed child attempt, retry exhaustion rejects with a failed child, and provider failures return null. Results commit on successful tool items in response order. Raw response and tool-output events let the entire admitted response finish before interruption; the last successful structured value wins. The retry cap stops later tools. A stream error after accepted output clears it and stops both provider reconnection and the runner’s outer retry; terminal failure cannot return stale output. Partial or invalid calls may recover, and completed ordinary tool effects persist. Concurrent threads own separate handlers. The legacy strict conversion and text parser remain only for session extensions. See [usage and migration](README.md).
- **Nested scoping and run-wide budget** (`runtime.js`). `human:` and `sess:` journal keys of a child workflow are prefixed with its scope path. `budget.spent()` is the whole run's spend (parent and children share `executionState`), excluding usage metered in the process before the run began. The ceiling is still checked before each start and, as in Claude 2.1.286, at combinator entry (`parallel()`/`pipeline()` throw once it is spent; agents inside a running combinator that hit it resolve `null`). Once usage reaches it, queued agents are withdrawn immediately instead of waiting for a slot. In-flight agents finish, so spend can still overshoot by what is already running.
- **Smaller fixes.**
  - Skip/retry controllers are registered at enqueue time: skip withdraws a queued agent, and retry of a queued agent is accepted as a no-op.
  - A user skip emits `end {status:'skipped', error:'skipped by user'}` and output state `skipped`.
  - `worktree.js` removes its temp folder when `git worktree add` fails.
  - `agentTypes.js` rejects names containing path separators or `..`, and maps the built-ins `general-purpose`, `Explore` and `Plan` to built-in prompts when no `.claude/agents` file overrides them. Explore and Plan also force a read-only sandbox.
  - `agentTypes.js` resolves an `agentType` by the definition's frontmatter `name:` (else the file name), searching every `.claude/agents` folder (subfolders included) from the cwd up to the git root, then `~/.claude/agents`, then the built-ins; frontmatter lists may be YAML flow or block lists. An unknown type throws Claude's `agent({agentType}): agent type 'X' not found. Available agents: …` before admission. The definition's `tools:` allowlist is enforced through `toolNarrowing.js` `allowlistExclusions()`: no write or shell tool runs the agent read-only on every core; on native Codex unlisted web search and MCP servers are turned off too.
  - `subagentPrompt.js` gives every agent Claude Code 2.1.280's workflow-subagent instructions as `developerInstructions` (text, StructuredOutput and JSON-fallback variants); an agentType's prompt gets the matching note appended.
  - `runtime.js` agent() rethrows configuration errors (`AgentConfigError`: unknown agentType, worktree setup, invalid schema) and, after five stall restarts (each logged `[stall] agent "X" stalled (no progress) after Ns — retrying (k/5)`), Claude's `agent stalled on all 6 attempts (no progress for Xms each)`. Only a user skip or a terminal provider error (logged `[label] failed: …`) resolves null.
  - `modelMap.js` treats Claude aliases as the session's model when the endpoint doesn't serve Codex's catalog (native Codex with a custom `model_provider`, from `config/read`, or a session model the catalog doesn't list).
  - `workflow-child.mjs` no longer pins the launch model, so a per-call `opts.model` wins over it, as in Claude Code.
  - `runWorkflow.js` installs a guest guard (before the generated intrinsics, which then freeze `Intl`): `Intl.DateTimeFormat#format()`/`formatToParts()` with no date throw like `Date.now()`. The shared generated `workflow-intrinsics.js` is unchanged.
  - The concurrency cap uses `os.availableParallelism()`.
  - `runtime.js` `CANCEL_GRACE_MS` is 6s: the app announces a stop under way (`{stopping:true}`) and then waits up to 8s before force-killing the runner, so slow worktree cleanup can finish.

## Local modifications (2026-10-06 Claude Code 2.1.280 configuration parity)

Regression tests: `app/tests/workflow-config.test.mjs`, `app/tests/workflow-tool-service.test.mjs` (fixture `app/tests/fixtures/workflow-runner-server.cjs`, whose prompts may now arrive framed).

- **Concurrency from the environment** (`runtime.js` `concurrencyCap`). `CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS` (an integer 1–256) sets the agent pool; otherwise `min(16, max(2, availableParallelism − 2))` (Claude's floor of 2, was 1). Code Desktop passes its Settings value through the same variable.
- **Stall watchdog 180s** (`runtime.js` `STALL_MS`, was 600s); still up to 5 restarts, `opts.stallMs` overrides.
- **Pause/resume** (`runtime.js` `setWorkflowPaused`, runtime `pause`). While paused, queued agents are not admitted; running agents finish. Used by Code Desktop's Tasks pane (/workflows "p").
- **Prompt provenance** (new `provenance.js`, `codexAgent.js`). With `CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_PROMPT_PROVENANCE` unset or truthy, an agent's prompt is sent inside Claude's "[Workflow harness — computed task]" frame with every line indented two spaces; `runtime.js` passes `framePrompt` and reports `promptFramed` accordingly. Journal identity still uses the unframed prompt. An isolated worktree adds Claude's worktree note after the prompt.
- **Same-prefix stagger** (`provenance.js` `PrefixStagger`, applied in `codexAgent.js`). Agents sharing a prompt-cache prefix (model, effort, agent type, schema, folder) wait up to `CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_PREFIX_STAGGER_MS` (default 5000; 0 with `DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING`) for the first one's first response; a prefix stays warm for 270s. Injected `runAgent` seams are not staggered.
- **Throttle backoff** (`codexAgent.js` `withRetry`). A rate-limited agent (429 / rate limit / overloaded codes or messages) waits 45s once (`retryAt` reaches the progress events) and is retried one time. Claude detects throttling from a degraded response instead; this runner keys on the provider's error.
- **Worktree names** (`worktree.js`, `codexAgent.js`). `isolation:'worktree'` folders are named `<runId>-<index>` when the run has an id.
- **Synchronous VM slice 30s** (`runWorkflow.js`, was 1s), as in Claude.
- **JSON fallback for cores without the StructuredOutput tool** (new `jsonAgent.js`, hook in `codexAgent.js` `runOneTurn`). With `opts.structuredOutput === false` (no structured output: ZCode, the ACP agents) or `'outputSchema'` (turn/start outputSchema only: the DeepSeek Harness, OpenCode/MiMo — the wire schema is also sent), a schema agent gets the author's JSON Schema in its prompt, its reply is parsed (strict, fenced or embedded JSON: `checkSchemaResult`) and validated with `schemaValidate.js`, and an invalid reply is answered in the same thread with the errors, up to `MAX_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_RETRIES` failed replies (default 5).
- **Subagent model** (`app/electron/workflow-child.mjs`, not this package): `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` (unless `inherit`) is the default agent model; `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE` pins it over per-call `opts.model`.
